credit_score.title: What Is a Credit Score?
credit_score.subtitle: Why lenders look at your history
cards: A credit score is a number (0–100) that shows how reliably you repay money. Sahoolat builds yours from non-traditional data.
Factors like utility bill consistency, land size, and committee reliability all contribute to your score — not just bank history.
A higher score means better access to microloans, lower interest rates, and faster approvals.
Your score updates automatically each time you log income, pay a committee cycle, or complete a crop season.
You can always see exactly why your score changed — every factor is explained in plain language.

quiz.q1: What does a higher credit score help you get?
quiz.q1_exp: A higher score gives lenders confidence to offer you better loan terms and faster approvals.
quiz.q2: Which of these does Sahoolat use to build your credit score?
quiz.q2_opt2: Utility bill consistency and committee reliability
quiz.q2_exp: Sahoolat uses non-traditional data — utilities, committee payments, land size — so unbanked users can build a score.
quiz.q3: How often does your score update?
quiz.q3_opt0: Automatically when you take actions like logging income
quiz.q3_opt2: Only when a bank requests it
quiz.q3_exp: Every income log, committee payment, or seasonal activity can update your score in real time.

committees.title: How Committees (BC) Work
committees.subtitle: Rotating savings — protect yourself
cards: A committee (BC/ROSCA) is a group where everyone contributes the same amount each cycle, and one member receives the full pot in turn.
The order of payout can be fixed (pre-agreed) or lottery-based. Fixed order is safer — get it in writing before joining.
Never join a committee without knowing all members, the cycle frequency, and the payout rules clearly.
Red flags: organizer asks for extra fees, refuses to share member list, or changes rules mid-cycle.
Sahoolat records your committee contributions and uses your on-time payment rate to improve your credit score.
If a member drops out, the remaining members must cover the shortfall — always know your liability.

quiz.q1_opt2: A rotating savings group where members take turns receiving the pot
quiz.q1_exp: A BC is a rotating savings group — all members contribute, and each takes the full pot in turn.
quiz.q2: Which payout order is generally safer?
quiz.q2_exp: A fixed, pre-agreed order prevents disputes and makes planning easier for all members.
quiz.q3: What is a red flag when joining a committee?
quiz.q3_opt0: The organizer provides a written member list
quiz.q3_opt1: The organizer charges extra hidden fees
quiz.q3_exp: Hidden fees, refusal to share member lists, or mid-cycle rule changes are serious red flags.
quiz.q4: How do committee payments affect your Sahoolat credit score?
quiz.q4_opt2: On-time contributions improve your reliability score
quiz.q4_exp: Consistent, on-time committee contributions are a positive signal that improves your credit profile.

saving_regularly.title: The Power of Saving Regularly
saving_regularly.subtitle: Small amounts, consistent habit
cards: Saving does not require a large income. Even Rs. 50–100 per day adds up to Rs. 1,500–3,000 per month.
Consistency matters more than amount. A daily Rs. 100 saver builds stronger habits than an occasional Rs. 1,000 deposit.
Sahoolat's Auto-Save feature automatically sets aside a percentage of each income you log — set it and forget it.
Your savings balance is always visible on your Wallet screen and contributes positively to your credit score.

quiz.q1: What matters more for building savings?
quiz.q1_opt0: Saving a very large amount once a year
quiz.q1_opt1: Saving small amounts consistently every day or week
quiz.q1_opt2: Waiting until you have spare money
quiz.q1_exp: Consistency builds the habit and compounds over time — small regular saves outperform irregular large ones.
quiz.q2_opt1: Sends money to a family member
quiz.q2_opt2: Transfers money to a bank automatically
quiz.q2_opt3: Sets aside a percentage of each income you log into your savings balance
quiz.q2_exp: Auto-Save deducts a percentage from each income log automatically so you save without thinking.
quiz.q3: How does saving regularly affect your credit score in Sahoolat?
quiz.q3_opt0: It has no effect on your score
quiz.q3_opt2: It contributes positively as a signal of financial discipline
quiz.q3_exp: Your savings rate (savings ÷ income over 90 days) is one of the credit score factors.

microloans.title: How Microloans Work
microloans.subtitle: Borrow smart — know the terms
cards: A microloan is a small loan (typically Rs. 10,000–500,000) from a microfinance institution (MFI) for income-generating purposes.
Interest can be charged as a flat fee on the full amount or on the declining balance. Declining balance is cheaper — always ask which method.
Before borrowing: confirm the total repayment amount, the number of installments, and any early repayment penalties.
Islamic / Qard-e-Hasna loans (like Akhuwat) charge zero interest — but have strict eligibility and community guarantor requirements.
Missing repayments damages your credit score and may trigger legal action. Only borrow what your monthly income can support.
Sahoolat shows you matched loan programs with their real eligibility criteria — check the Loan Matcher screen.

quiz.q1: What is a microloan typically used for?
quiz.q1_opt2: Income-generating activities like farming or small business
quiz.q1_exp: Microloans are designed for productive, income-generating uses — not consumption.
quiz.q2: Which interest calculation method is cheaper for the borrower?
quiz.q2_exp: Declining balance charges interest only on the remaining principal — significantly cheaper than flat rate.
quiz.q3: What should you confirm before signing a loan agreement?
quiz.q3_opt0: Total repayment amount, installments, and penalty clauses
quiz.q3_exp: Always verify total cost, repayment schedule, and any early or late payment penalties before signing.
quiz.q4: What happens if you miss microloan repayments?
quiz.q4_opt3: Your credit score is damaged and legal action may follow
quiz.q4_exp: Missed payments damage your credit history and can lead to legal or community-based consequences.
quiz.q5_opt0: They have the highest interest rates
quiz.q5_exp: Akhuwat offers interest-free loans under the Islamic Qard-e-Hasna model, requiring community guarantors.

crop_insurance.title: Parametric Crop Insurance
crop_insurance.subtitle: Weather-based automatic protection
cards: Parametric crop insurance pays out automatically when a measurable weather event (like extreme heat or flood) crosses a pre-set threshold — no claim filing needed.
You choose: crop type, district, the threshold type (heat, rainfall, drought, frost), and the threshold value.
When the weather data breaches your threshold, a payout event is logged immediately — transparent and rule-based.
Sahoolat uses Open-Meteo weather API to check real daily readings for Pakistani agricultural districts.
This is simulated for demo — in a real deployment, the payout would be transferred to your linked account via a partner insurer.

quiz.q1: What triggers a payout in parametric crop insurance?
quiz.q1_opt0: A manual claim submitted by the farmer
quiz.q1_opt2: A measurable weather event crossing a pre-set threshold
quiz.q1_opt3: Crop market price falling below a level
quiz.q1_exp: Parametric insurance triggers automatically when weather data crosses your chosen threshold — no claims process needed.
quiz.q2: Which of these is a valid threshold type in Sahoolat?
quiz.q2_exp: Sahoolat supports four types: extreme heat, heavy rainfall, drought, and frost (low temperature).
quiz.q3: What data source does Sahoolat use for weather readings?
quiz.q3_opt3: Open-Meteo API with real district coordinates
quiz.q3_exp: Sahoolat uses the Open-Meteo free API with GPS coordinates for Pakistani agricultural districts.
quiz.q4: Why is parametric insurance faster than traditional crop insurance?
quiz.q4_opt1: It needs a field inspection first
quiz.q4_opt3: The payout triggers automatically from objective weather data — no claim or inspection needed
quiz.q4_exp: No claims adjuster, no paperwork — the rule-based engine pays automatically when the threshold is crossed.

govt_schemes.title: BISP & Kissan Card Eligibility
govt_schemes.subtitle: Know your rights to government support
cards: The Punjab Kissan Card offers interest-free crop loans up to Rs. 150,000 for farmers with 1–12.5 acres of PLRA-registered land.
BISP Benazir Kafaalat provides Rs. 13,500 quarterly to female heads of low-income households with an NSER PMT score ≤ 32.
To check BISP eligibility: SMS your CNIC (no dashes) to 8171 or visit 8171.bisp.gov.pk.
To check Kissan Card eligibility: SMS your CNIC to 8070 or visit agripunjab.gov.pk.
Sahoolat's Gov Scheme Bot asks you a short set of questions and shows you exactly which criteria you meet or miss — transparently.

quiz.q1: What is the BISP Benazir Kafaalat quarterly payment amount (as of Jan 2025)?
quiz.q1_exp: BISP increased the quarterly stipend to Rs. 13,500 in January 2025. Check bisp.gov.pk for latest updates.
quiz.q2: How do you check your BISP eligibility using SMS?
quiz.q2_exp: Text your 13-digit CNIC (no dashes) to 8171 to get your BISP eligibility status via SMS.
quiz.q3: Which landholding range qualifies for the Punjab Kissan Card?
quiz.q3_exp: The Kissan Card requires PLRA-registered landholding between 1.0 and 12.5 acres.
quiz.q4: Which group is EXCLUDED from BISP cash transfers?
quiz.q4_opt1: Active government employees or tax filers
quiz.q4_exp: Government employees, tax filers, car owners, and those with international travel history are excluded from BISP.

fraud_awareness.title: Recognizing Financial Fraud
fraud_awareness.subtitle: Protect yourself from scams
cards: Common scam: someone calls saying you won a prize and asks for your CNIC, OTP, or bank PIN. Real organizations NEVER ask for these by phone.
Never share your OTP with anyone — not even someone claiming to be from your bank, Sahoolat, BISP, or the government.
Fake BISP agents charge fees to 'register' you. BISP registration is completely free. Report imposters to 0800-26477.
Loan scams: someone offers an 'easy loan' with no documentation but asks for an advance fee. Legitimate MFIs never ask for fees before disbursement.
If someone pressures you to decide immediately about money — that is a manipulation tactic. Pause, verify independently, then decide.

quiz.q1: Someone calls you claiming to be from BISP and asks for your OTP to 'activate your payment'. What do you do?
quiz.q1_opt0: Share the OTP quickly so you don't miss your payment
quiz.q1_opt1: Ask them to call back later
quiz.q1_opt2: Give only the last 4 digits of your CNIC
quiz.q1_opt3: Hang up — real BISP never asks for OTPs by phone
quiz.q1_exp: BISP and legitimate organizations never ask for OTPs, PINs, or passwords over the phone. Always hang up.
quiz.q2: How much does BISP charge to register a new beneficiary?
quiz.q2_opt2: Zero — BISP registration is completely free
quiz.q2_opt3: A percentage of the first payment
quiz.q2_exp: BISP registration is 100% free. Anyone charging a fee for BISP registration is committing fraud.
quiz.q3: What is a sign that a loan offer is a scam?
quiz.q3_opt0: They have a physical office address
quiz.q3_opt1: The lender asks for an advance fee before disbursing your loan
quiz.q3_opt2: They ask to see your CNIC
quiz.q3_exp: Legitimate lenders never ask for money before giving you the loan. Advance fee = fraud.
quiz.q4: Someone pressures you to send money 'right now or the offer expires'. What is this?
quiz.q4_opt2: A manipulation tactic used by scammers
quiz.q4_exp: Urgency pressure is a classic manipulation tactic. Always pause, verify independently, then decide.
quiz.q5: What should you NEVER share, even with someone claiming to be from your bank?
quiz.q5_opt2: Your account number if already known to them
quiz.q5_exp: Your OTP, PIN, and password are secrets only you should know — no legitimate organization needs them.

budgeting_irregular.title: Budgeting on Irregular Income
budgeting_irregular.subtitle: Plan when income is unpredictable
cards: Irregular income means some weeks or months you earn more, some less. The key is budgeting around your MINIMUM expected income, not the average.
Step 1: List essential expenses (rent, food, school fees, utilities). This is your survival floor — always cover this first.
Step 2: In high-income months, save the surplus rather than spending it. Build a buffer equal to one month's essential expenses.
Step 3: Separate 'wants' from 'needs'. Wants are delayed until your buffer is full.
Use Sahoolat's income logging to track your actual monthly income pattern over 3–6 months to see your real average.
Review your budget every month — irregular income means your plan should flex, not be rigid.

quiz.q1: When budgeting on irregular income, you should base your plan on:
quiz.q1_exp: Plan for your minimum income so you can always cover essentials, then save any surplus.
quiz.q2: What should you build first from surplus income?
quiz.q2_opt2: A buffer of one month's essential expenses
quiz.q2_exp: A one-month buffer is your financial safety net — build it before spending on wants.
quiz.q3: What is the 'survival floor' in budgeting?
quiz.q3_opt1: The maximum you can spend on food
quiz.q3_opt2: The ground floor of your house
quiz.q3_opt3: The minimum essential monthly expenses you must always cover
quiz.q3_exp: Your survival floor is rent + food + school + utilities — the non-negotiable minimum every month.
quiz.q4: How does Sahoolat help you understand your income pattern?
quiz.q4_opt0: It predicts next month's income using AI
quiz.q4_opt1: It connects to your bank automatically
quiz.q4_opt2: It asks your employer for salary records
quiz.q4_opt3: It logs each income entry and shows a 6-month trend chart
quiz.q4_exp: The Wallet screen's trend chart shows your real income pattern over 6 months — helping you see your true average.

digital_banking.title: Getting Started with Digital Banking
digital_banking.subtitle: Safe steps for first-time users
cards: Digital banking lets you check your balance, transfer money, and pay bills without visiting a branch — through mobile apps or SMS services.
Safe first step: open a Meezan Bank, HBL, or Bank Alfalah account with your CNIC at a branch — then activate mobile banking.
Never access your bank app on someone else's phone or a shared device. Always log out after each session.
Your bank will NEVER ask for your PIN, password, or OTP over the phone. If they do — it is a scam.
JazzCash and Easypaisa are mobile wallets — useful for small transfers but not a replacement for a proper savings account.

quiz.q1: What is the safest first step toward digital banking?
quiz.q1_opt0: Download an app you found on social media
quiz.q1_opt1: Give your CNIC to a street agent to open an account
quiz.q1_opt2: Open an account in person at a licensed bank branch with your CNIC
quiz.q1_opt3: Share your personal details with a WhatsApp group
quiz.q1_exp: Open accounts in person at licensed banks — never through unverified agents or social media links.
quiz.q2: You receive a call from someone claiming to be your bank asking for your PIN. What do you do?
quiz.q2_opt0: Share only the first two digits
quiz.q2_opt1: Hang up — banks never ask for PINs by phone
quiz.q2_opt2: Share it since they are the bank
quiz.q2_opt3: Text your PIN to their number instead
quiz.q2_exp: No legitimate bank ever asks for your PIN, password, or OTP over the phone. Always hang up.
quiz.q3: What should you do after using mobile banking on a shared device?
quiz.q3_opt2: Always manually log out and clear saved credentials
quiz.q3_exp: Always log out manually on shared devices — auto-logout is not guaranteed on all apps.

family_financial_goals.title: Setting Family Financial Goals
family_financial_goals.subtitle: Plan together, achieve together
cards: A family financial goal is a specific, measurable target: 'Save Rs. 50,000 for school fees by March' — not just 'save more money'.
Involve the whole family in setting goals. When everyone understands the target, everyone is more careful with daily spending.
Prioritize goals: emergency fund first, then education, then home improvement, then aspirational goals.
Break large goals into monthly milestones. Rs. 50,000 in 10 months = Rs. 5,000 per month.
Review goals every month — life changes, income changes, and your goals should adapt without giving up entirely.

quiz.q1: Which is a good family financial goal?
quiz.q1_opt2: Save Rs. 60,000 for Eid expenses by saving Rs. 5,000/month for 12 months
quiz.q1_exp: Good goals are specific, measurable, and time-bound — they tell you exactly how much and by when.
quiz.q2: What should be the FIRST priority goal for most families?
quiz.q2_opt2: An emergency fund covering one month's expenses
quiz.q2_exp: An emergency fund is the foundation — without it, any unexpected expense can derail all other goals.
quiz.q3: How do you make a large financial goal less overwhelming?
quiz.q3_opt0: Ignore it until you have enough money
quiz.q3_exp: Breaking a large goal into monthly targets makes it manageable and gives you regular checkpoints.
quiz.q4: Why should family goals be reviewed monthly?
quiz.q4_opt0: To add more goals each month
quiz.q4_opt1: To find reasons to give up
quiz.q4_opt2: Because life and income change — goals should adapt without abandoning the plan entirely
quiz.q4_opt3: Monthly review is a government requirement
quiz.q4_exp: Flexible goals survive real life. Rigid plans that can't adapt often get abandoned entirely.
